items.title: dsh-superagent-prototype
items.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
items.summary: DeepSeek AI published dsh-superagent, a proactive coding agent prototype for DeepSeek Harness, on GitHub on 2026-10-31. The team describes it as research code from day-to-day development work, not an official DeepSeek product, and much of the engineering was completed by coding agents. The prototype listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu; when an authorized person requests work, it opens a work item, processes it in its own session, and answers in the original conversation with a pull request. The design follows the rule of taking as little human attention as possible and delivering as much value as possible. The code is intended for reference and adaptation, not as a production product.

items.summary: agent-autoloop is an open-source AI agents skill designed to enhance command-line AI agents like Claude Code and Codex CLI. It allows these agents to operate autonomously in the background, picking up tasks on a schedule and handling them independently. When it encounters tasks that require human intervention, such as deleting data or making financial transactions, it sends a notification to the user for approval. This setup aims to provide a more efficient and less intrusive way of managing tasks with command-line AI agents.

It requires Windows 10/11, Google Chrome, and Python 3.10 or higher. The tool automates the subscription process by binding a provided credit card with zero cost protection, importing Google accounts, and leveraging free trial periods to extend the subscription up to 24 months. The script also includes a feature to cancel auto-renewal to lock in the benefits. The log indicates the tool is set to last until October 2028. The blog post provides an analysis of the tool's functionality, confirming its aim to automate the subscription process.

items.title: FlashProve
items.description: A research prototype for zero-knowledge proofs of AI inference. Not maintained.
items.summary: FlashProve is a research prototype for zero-knowledge proofs of AI inference, open-sourced by Anthropic. It is not maintained. The GitHub repository for FlashProve lists it as a prototype and provides details about its latest commit, history, and usage. The project has 40 stars and 0 watchers on one GitHub page, while another GitHub page shows 721 stars and 2 watchers. The system can generate proofs for Meta’s 400-billion-parameter Llama 4 Maverick model at approximately 110 tokens per second on a single H100 GPU, with each proof sized at about 19 MB. The project employs cryptographic methods derived from blockchain ZK technology, enabling users to verify AI outputs without needing access to the model weights or re-running the model.

items.title: verdict
items.description: A 197 KB local semantic verifier for AI agent tool calls. Exit code 0 is not proof.
items.summary: The sources describe "Verdict" as a 197 KB local semantic verifier for AI agent tool calls, which reads a CLI tool call and returns `success`, `failure`, `blocked`, or `unknown`. It operates locally on CPU with no Python dependencies, using a model architecture based on hashed character 3–5-grams and word 1–3-grams → multiclass logistic regression. The verifier has 196,608 int8 weights and runs without network calls or telemetry. The GitHub repository reports 217 stars and 2 watchers, with no forks. The demo results show the system rejecting all 11 misreporting agents in five runs without wrongly rejecting any honest claims. The paper emphasizes that verification is read-only and does not modify state, ensuring safety and correctness in system behavior.
